  "title": "Americas Crypto & Exchanges: Overviewing the SEC innovation exemption order permitting trading of tokenized equities",
  "type": "crypto",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-09-19",
  "insights": [
   "On 9/17, the SEC issued a 5-year conditional exemption allowing tokenized securities venues (TSVs) to offer tokenized equities in the US, provided they use automated market maker (AMM) order books.",
   "The exemption is limited to native tokenized equities that offer shareholder rights and dividends comparable to traditional stock, excluding non-native derivative-like products.",
   "TSVs must provide written notice to issuers, who retain the right to object to the tokenization of their securities, potentially limiting the total addressable market.",
   "The AMM requirement targets smaller, nascent DeFi venues, as traditional exchanges and centralized crypto platforms currently rely on central limit order books (CLOBs).",
   "Goldman Sachs views this as a competitive positive for traditional exchanges like NDAQ and ICE, as it avoids broader, more disruptive tokenization legislation like the failed CLARITY Act.",
   "COIN is identified as a primary beneficiary due to its existing brokerage product alignment and infrastructure offerings, though it would need to build AMM-based exchange technology to utilize the exemption.",
   "HOOD could benefit but would require significant product development to transition its non-native international tokenized equity product to the native standard required by the SEC order.",
   "The order may drive increased stablecoin adoption (USDC) as tokenized equities on-chain require tokenized cash for settlement.",
   "Traditional exchanges (NDAQ, ICE) are unlikely to adopt this TSV model, preferring their existing market infrastructure frameworks and DTC-eligible pilot programs."
  ],
